name: PT Abadi Lestari Indonesia Tbk

frontmatter.title: Abadi Lestari: a bird's-nest exporter priced as a platform
frontmatter.summary: We initiate at SELL. The fundamental DCF value is Rp83, a fraction of the Rp2,250 quote, and the house konglo lens lifts the twelve-month target to Rp1,112 only because the float, not the business, sets this price. Earnings are real but cash is not: receivables and inventories absorb most of a year's sales. Return -50.6%.
thesis: The business is a genuine exporter of processed edible bird's nest with a small but fast-growing consumer arm, and its nine-month margin improved on cost control [S2, S5].

It does not convert that profit into cash: operating cash flow was negative in each of the last three fiscal years and again in the nine months [S7, S5], because customers are carried for months and inventories are large.
Four customers took most of FY2025 sales, all of them Chinese or Hong Kong traders [S7], so the sector-wide Chinese import suspension is a direct revenue risk [S8].
The equity is not cheap on any fundamental measure: the pack's trailing multiples are in the stratosphere and the market value sits far above our DCF [S0].

The float is the price setter: the controlling shareholder held almost all the stock before the IPO, the free float is thin, and the shares traded at many multiples of the offer price within weeks of listing [S9, S0].

catalysts.event: Free-float step: the exchange requires a higher public float, forcing a sell-down or new shares
Nine-month results published; the company guides on cost efficiency and consumer launches
FY2026 audited accounts, the first full year as a listed company

blocks.text: We initiate coverage of PT Abadi Lestari Indonesia at **SELL** with a twelve-month target of Rp1,112, against a last price of Rp2,250 — a total return of -50.6%. The target is the house konglo lens applied to a fundamental value of Rp83: the lens keeps part of the market's premium for twelve months rather than pretending it disappears overnight, and it is explained in the valuation and governance sections.

The variant view is not that the company is a fraud or that the nest business is worthless. It is that the market is pricing a cash-generative consumer franchise that the accounts do not describe. The company earns a real profit — IDR40.9bn attributable in FY2025 [S7] — while consuming operating cash, and the gap is working capital, not accounting trickery alone. Receivables and inventories together are larger than a full year of sales [S7], which is what an export business selling to a handful of trading houses on long credit looks like.

What moves the value, in order: the cash-conversion cycle (a permanent reduction in receivable days would be worth more than any plausible sales growth); the Chinese import access that the quarantine authority says is still restricted [S8]; and the consumer segment's margin mix, which is the only part of the business earning a return that covers its cost of capital [S2, S7].

Edible bird's nest is a Chinese-Indonesian specialty food, harvested from swiftlet houses and cleaned
for sale as a premium tonic. Indonesia is the largest producer, and the trade runs through a small
number of licensed exporters into Hong Kong and mainland China, where the end market is gift-driven
and highly seasonal around the lunar new year. Official market access is bilateral: the Chinese customs
authority registers each foreign plant, so a registration problem is a company-level revenue event,
not a price event.

The company processes and sells edible bird's nest and, more recently, a range of ready-to-drink and ready-to-eat products under its own brands [S3]. Two segments carry the accounts: processed nest, which was the great majority of the FY2025 total, and consumer goods, which contributed IDR104.6bn in FY2025 against roughly half that a year earlier [S7]. The mix then moved sharply AGAINST consumer: in the nine months of 2026 consumer-goods revenue fell by roughly a third, to IDR45.4bn from IDR69.0bn, taking its share of sales from about a sixth to roughly a tenth, while processed nest was flat at IDR379.2bn against IDR379.2bn [S5, note 20]. The consumer line still earns a gross margin in the high forties against a nest margin in the high teens [S2], but it is the smaller leg and it is shrinking.

The customer base is the defining feature. In FY2025 the four largest customers — all trading houses in China or Hong Kong — took 76.0% of sales, and the largest alone took 30.0% [S7]. Sales are therefore negotiated with a handful of counterparties, shipped on credit, and exposed to the renminbi and dollar crosses; the receivable balance of IDR84.2bn from related parties and IDR189.3bn from third parties is the visible consequence [S7].

The stated strategy is to deepen export penetration in China, open Vietnam and Thailand, push value-added nest products under a "premium affordable" positioning, and grow the consumer brands [S3]. The consumer arm is the diversification leg and the phytopharmaceutical work is an early-stage option: the company capitalised intangible spending on it during the current year [S5, S2].

Ownership is concentrated. PT Realco Omega Investama held almost all the shares before the IPO, the founder-family directors hold the balance, and the December 2025 offering sold a fifth of the enlarged capital to the public at Rp168 a share [S9, S7]. Post-listing the controller and affiliates still hold the great majority of the register [S0].

The industry's economics are set by two things the company does not control: Chinese import registration and the price of raw nest at the swiftlet-house gate. The first has just turned adverse. The Indonesian quarantine agency confirms that the Chinese customs authority suspended a tranche of Indonesian nest exporters over aluminium content above the Chinese limit, that the suspension is officially still in place, and that negotiation is under way with no announced resolution [S8]. The agency has tightened domestic quality control in parallel. The partial offset is the domestic pivot that the same article links — RLCO opening the local market with a global-standard product [S8] — and it is visible in the filed numbers: processed-nest revenue was flat year on year at IDR379.2bn against IDR379.2bn with the suspension already in force [S5, note 20]. No archived source quantifies the domestic channel's volume, price or margin, so we carry it qualitatively and in the bull case rather than as a base-case uplift.

The second is the raw-material cycle. Raw nest purchases were IDR379.2bn in FY2025, the bulk of cost of goods sold [S7], and the company has no disclosed upstream integration, no volume series and no long-term supply contract in the filings we read. It is therefore a price taker on its input and, because its customers are trading houses rather than retail brands, largely a price taker on its output. The one genuine source of pricing power is the branded consumer line, which earns a gross margin roughly two and a half times the nest segment's [S2] — that is where any moat would have to be built.

Competitive position: the company is a mid-sized processor, not the largest, and its filings disclose no market share [S3, S7]. The moat, on the evidence, is thin — registration and relationships with a few trading houses, plus a domestic brand that is still small. Our five-forces reading: supplier power high (unintegrated raw material), buyer power very high (four customers, most of sales), new-entrant threat moderate (registration is a barrier but not a proprietary one), substitution low (nest is a culturally specific product), rivalry moderate. The industry deck's agri curves do not price this company's inputs, which is why we switch both cost links off in the model.

Regulation beyond China access is the ordinary Indonesian set: a listed company with a controlling shareholder, an audit committee, and the exchange's free-float rules now bearing on the register [S9].

**Revenue.** FY2025 sales were IDR635.2bn, up from IDR530.4bn [S7]. The nine months of 2026 fell to IDR424.6bn against the prior-year comparative [S5], but with a better gross margin: IDR117.9bn of FY2025 gross profit on an eighteen-and-a-half per cent margin became a twenty-per-cent margin on the nine-month number [S5, S7]. The segment detail is the load-bearing fact: processed nest was flat at IDR379.2bn against IDR379.2bn, while consumer goods fell by roughly a third to IDR45.4bn from IDR69.0bn [S5, note 20]. Our FY2026E of IDR611.7bn holds the fourth quarter at the prior year's fourth-quarter level rather than extrapolating the nine-month decline, because the fourth quarter is seasonally the largest in both disclosed years [S7, S5]. Beyond it we do NOT return to the previous draft's eight per cent: with the bulk segment flat and the high-margin leg contracting, we model total growth of 2.0% in FY2027E, 2.5% and 3.0%, fading to the house long-run rate. Export penetration, the domestic pivot and the IPO proceeds are upside in the bull case, not assumptions in the base without a witnessed turn [S3, S8, S9].

**Margins and costs.** The margin gain did not come from the consumer mix, which was a drag as that segment's share fell: it came from the processed-nest segment's own margin, seventeen per cent in the nine months against fourteen per cent a year earlier, and from the twenty-eight-billion-rupiah cost-savings programme [S2, S5]. We hold the witnessed 20.1% through FY2027E and fade it gently to 19.9%, because the one-off nest-margin step is not sourced to repeat and the contracting consumer leg keeps the mix against us. Operating costs are held at the witnessed nine-month ratio of 4.8% [S5]. The company's cost saving is real: general and administrative expense fell year on year in the nine months and management quantifies the programme in its own statement [S2].

**Cash flow, working capital and debt.** This is where the accounts and the story part company. Operating cash flow was negative in FY2025 at IDR-30.7bn [S7] and negative again in the nine months at IDR-44.2bn [S5], despite positive net profit both times (IDR40.9bn and IDR24.1bn respectively) [S7, S5]. Cash received from customers was IDR592.6bn against sales of IDR635.2bn, and the nine-month receipts line is similarly short of the revenue line [S7, S5]. Inventories of IDR281.3bn and receivables of IDR84.2bn plus IDR189.3bn are not a timing artefact of one year: the balance sheet is a permanently funded asset, and it is funded with bank debt — short-term facilities, a current maturity and a small long-term tranche, with finance charges of IDR37.7bn in FY2025 alone [S7].

We model working capital at 102.0% of sales in FY2026E, i.e. as a further OUTFLOW rather than a release, and hold that ratio flat through the forecast and the terminal year. The previous draft held a fixed ratio below the FY2025 actual, which mechanically released cash on a falling revenue line and put the first discounted year at the opposite sign to the filed nine months; that is corrected here, and the intermediate revision that faded the ratio back toward the FY2025 audited level by FY2028E is corrected too, because no filing shows receivable or inventory days falling — the filed direction is the other way, from the audited ratio to about 102.0% at 30 September [S5, note 6, S7]. The forecast therefore consumes working capital every year, with a build of IDR47.8bn in FY2026E, IDR12.5bn in FY2027E and IDR15.9bn in FY2028E. FY2026E free cash flow is IDR23.0bn after that build, consistent in direction with the IDR-44.2bn nine-month operating cash flow [S5, F29]. Capex is held near the recurring rate of about two and a half per cent of sales; the IPO proceeds are not assigned by any source to a specific capacity step, so we do not carry an uplift for it [S9, F33, S7]. EBITDA in this report is EBIT plus depreciation and amortisation, excluding other income, which is why FY2025A EBITDA is IDR99.6bn rather than the IDR85.6bn EBIT plus D&A plus the other-income line [S7].

**Earnings-quality flags.** The screens in the house card: - *Accruals.* Net profit has outrun cash every year of the disclosed history; the gap is working capital rather than a single accrual, and it is growing with the receivable balance [S7, S5]. - *Divergence.* Receivables grew faster than revenue in the current year, and inventories did so as well [S7, S5] — the textbook pattern of sales recognised ahead of collection. - *IDX regime.* The shares listed only in December 2025, were flagged for unusual market activity within days of listing, and trade with a thin free float [S9, S0]. No special-notation letters or special-monitoring-board status are disclosed in the filings we read. - *Related parties.* A material related-party receivable sits alongside a related-party payable that was repaid during FY2025 [S7]; the flows are disclosed and quantified, not hidden. - *Restatement.* The data pack carries depreciation of IDR14.0bn for FY2025 against the LK's charge, because the IDX cash-flow feed is direct-method; we restate it, and we also restate net profit for the common-control proforma adjustment the pack ignores [S7].
No confirmed manipulation-class flag emerged from these screens; the flags are optics-class and disclosed, and they are priced by the cash-flow model rather than by a haircut to the P&L [S7].

The method set is the industry default: a discounted cash flow as primary, with an earnings and an EV/EBITDA cross-check. For a business whose profit is real but whose cash is not, an earnings multiple is the wrong primary — it capitalises the very accrual that the cash flow denies. The DCF therefore carries 80.0% of the blend, with 10.0% on the earnings cross-check and 10.0% on EV/EBITDA — the two cross-checks are read as a sanity band, not as support.

Our cost of capital is built from the house framework and lands at 11.9% with a cost of equity of 12.2%. That is inside the house rupiah band, at the upper end, which is where a levered micro-cap with a concentrated register belongs; the beta is the industry default because the shares have too short a history to estimate one [S0]. Terminal growth is 4.0%, the house long-run rate; we retain it because it is below the observed revenue rate, but the moat is thin and the business is funded by working capital, so there is no case for more. The terminal value is a little over half of enterprise value — but this is NOT an asset-light business: operating working capital is about ninety per cent of sales [S7, F15, F16, F17], and the terminal value is supported by a business that must fund receivables and inventory before it earns. The sensitivity table shows what happens if the terminal is wrong.

The multiple-survival test: the terminal value divided by terminal EBIT implies an exit EV/EBIT BELOW the IDR671.2bn entry EV over FY2026E EBIT of IDR93.3bn — the DCF fades the multiple rather than assuming expansion. Growth is manufactured, not declared: capex less depreciation plus the working-capital build absorbs most of NOPAT through the forecast, and the modest incremental returns that capital earns are why we model low single-digit growth, not the double-digit path the previous draft assumed.

The cross-checks are peer-median multiples — 4.14 times earnings and 4.69 times EV/EBITDA — drawn from corn-and-soymeal feed millers with twenty-per-cent gross margins, not from a bird's-nest processor earning a consumer gross margin in the high forties. They are not comparable to a bird-nest processor, which is why each carries only 10.0% of the blend and the DCF keeps 80.0%; RLCO's own trailing multiples are far higher because the quote ran ahead of the IPO offer price, so the divergence is between a wrong peer set and a stretched market price, not a hidden value estimate [S0, S9]. We show the cross-checks for completeness and do not let them set the answer. The P/E cross-check sits -31.5% from the DCF and EV/EBITDA -82.5%, which we attribute to the wrong peer set rather than to a hidden value estimate.

What the price implies: at Rp2,250 the market is capitalising 30.35 times our fundamental value of Rp83. Reverse-engineered, the growth and margin pair needed to justify the quote is far outside anything the filings describe — the reverse-DCF line in the sensitivity table says so. We would need the cash cycle to invert and the consumer segment to become the majority of sales and the Chinese access problem to vanish, simultaneously, to get close.

**The konglo lens.** Because this is a concentrated-ownership name, the target is not the fundamental value: the lens measures the market's premium and holds a probability-weighted share of it for twelve months. The quote of Rp2,250 is 30.35 times the probability-weighted fundamental value of Rp74 a share; the compression share rises with the name's flags — high-shareholding-concentration status and a free-float step due inside the window, 10.0% of extra closing share between them [house konglo registry, as-of 27 October 2026]. Applying the same premium-kept arithmetic to our twelve-month fundamental value of Rp83 gives a base-regime price of Rp645, a bear-regime price of Rp165 and a bull-regime price of Rp2,994; the probability-weighted target is Rp1,112, above fundamental value and still well below the quote. This is a statement about how fast a thin float re-rates, not a second opinion on the business.

Risks, by likelihood and impact: - **Chinese market access — high likelihood, high impact.** The customs suspension is officially still in force and unresolved [S8]; with four customers at most of sales [S7], a single blocked buyer removes a large share of revenue. - **Cash conversion and refinancing — high likelihood, high impact.** Working capital is 102.0% of sales and funded by short-term bank lines [S7, S5]; a roll-over failure is a solvency event, not a valuation event. - **Customer concentration — high likelihood, medium impact.** Disclosed above; the company has no long-term contracts in the filings. - **Raw-material price — medium likelihood, medium impact.** Unintegrated, price-taking buyer of raw nest [S7]. - **Governance and float — medium likelihood, medium impact.** Controlling shareholder, thin float, a free-float deadline that forces supply [S9, S0]. - **Liquidity — medium likelihood, medium impact.** Turnover is adequate for a small position but the register is thin; the engine charges a liquidity discount of 0.0% because the ADTV sits above the house threshold [S0]. - **Currency — medium likelihood, low impact.** Export receipts are foreign-currency; no hedge is disclosed [S7].

**Inventory realisability.** The auditor names inventories as a key audit matter, and they are IDR319.9bn at 30 September, more than a third of total assets and about eight months of annualised cost of goods sold, with the consumer finished-goods line already falling [S5, note 6, F36]. They also secure the short-term bank lines [S5]. A ten-to-twenty per cent write-down takes off roughly a tenth to a fifth of inventory in equity and, because the same inventory is loan collateral, is a creditor event as much as an earnings one. We carry the stress in the bear case and in the sensitivity table; the base case assumes the book value is realisable, which the auditor's unmodified opinion supports.

The konglo lens is the reason the target sits above fundamental value. The market pays 30.35 times what the business is worth; the lens keeps a probability-weighted share of that premium for twelve months by closing 40.0% of the log gap in the base regulatory regime. The compression is faster because the name carries the high-shareholding-concentration flag and a free-float step inside the window [house konglo registry, as-of 27 October 2026, recording the exchange HSC release of 22 October 2026]. The REGIME scenarios are separate from the business scenarios and carry their own twenty-five/fifty/twenty-five weights (bear/base/bull). In the bear regime the lens closes 80.0% of the gap and the target lands at Rp165, about twice the fundamental value of Rp83 — the premium is cut sharply, not "kept almost whole". In the bull regime the gap is allowed to widen slightly, which is why the bull target exceeds today's quote.

The business scenarios carry the thirty/fifty/twenty weights below. Bear (30.0%): China access closes for this company's buyers, revenue falls rather than grows, and the margin gives back the nine-month gain; the cash cycle then consumes the balance sheet while debt service continues [S8, S7]. Bull (20.0%): the consumer leg stabilises, the domestic pivot and the reopened export channel lift processed-nest volume, phytopharmaceutical and new brand launches land, and the margin adds three points ON TOP of the achieved nine-month rate — in line with the three-point processed-nest gain (seventeen per cent against fourteen per cent) and above the two-point blended delta, so the bull is not thinner than the last actual improvement [S2, S5, S8]. The shocks are NOT mirrored on revenue — the bear takes thirteen points off growth, the bull adds three — because a blocked buyer is a discrete step change while the upside is incremental; both margin shocks are three points. The asymmetry in the outcomes comes from the operating leverage in the cash cycle, not from a stacked bear case.

Signposts that would change the view: a filed resolution of the Chinese suspension naming the company or its customers [S8]; a marked fall in receivable days in a quarterly filing [S5]; the consumer segment passing a quarter of sales at its current margin [S2]; and any dividend declaration, which would signal the cash cycle has turned [S7].

Control sits with PT Realco Omega Investama [S9], and the board is young and founder-led — the president director is also the controlling mind behind the operating subsidiary [S9]. The non-executive layer is credible: a former state-bank chief executive chairs the commissioners and an independent commissioner with a capital-markets background sits alongside [S9]. The auditor is Krisnawan, Nugroho & Fahmy, whose report is unmodified but names inventories — a third of total assets — as a key audit matter [S7]. We read that as appropriate rather than alarming: the inventory is the business.

Related-party dealings are NOT immaterial: trade receivables from related parties are IDR84.2bn, about thirty-one per cent of total receivables and about thirteen per cent of FY2025 revenue [S7, F16, F17]. The counterparties are named in the related-party note — PT Realfood Karya Indonesia, PT Eling Janji Pertama, PT Hidup Melawan Waktu and PT Bahagia Elok Sentosa, all controlled by the same ultimate shareholder, with the consumer-products sales booked through the RWA subsidiary to those affiliates [S7, the related-party note]. A related-party payable of IDR70.0bn was repaid in cash during FY2025 [S7, F25]. This is the modal value-destruction channel on IDX, so the bear case carries it: if the affiliate receivables are not collected, the loss is a fifth of equity. We found no pledge of the controlling stake, no serial rights issue and no auditor down-tier in the filings reviewed; the share-count change is the IPO and a share dividend, both sourced [S7, S9].

**Konglo profile.** Control is PT Realco Omega Investama, which held almost all the shares before the December 2025 IPO and sold a fifth of the enlarged capital at Rp168, leaving the controller and affiliates with the great majority; no other holder above five per cent is disclosed in the filings reviewed [S9, F32, F33, F34]. The free float is 13.5% against the 15.0% requirement due by 31 March 2027, so a sell-down or new shares are a dated supply event [house konglo registry, as-of 27 October 2026]. The name is on the exchange's HSC list and is therefore excluded from the IHSG calculation and from the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI indexes [house konglo registry, as-of 27 October 2026, which records the exchange HSC list of 22 October 2026 and its index consequences]; the registry shows no name-specific index deletion and no enforcement action against the company [konglo registry]. Dividend policy is effectively nil: the only distribution is a share dividend, and cash payout is not fundable while operating cash flow is negative [S7, F35].

Dividends: none in cash. The only distribution in the statement of changes in equity is a share dividend [S7], and with operating cash flow negative the base case carries no cash payout. The free-float step is the governance event to watch: the name sits on the exchange's high-shareholding-concentration list and must raise its public float, currently 13.5% against a 15.0% requirement, inside the window [house konglo registry, as-of 27 October 2026]. That is a supply event with a date, and it is why the lens compresses the premium rather than preserving it.

ESG: the material exposure is product-safety compliance — the Chinese aluminium limit is an ESG issue that became a revenue issue [S8]. Swiftlet-house sourcing carries biodiversity and animal-welfare scrutiny, and the company publishes a sustainability report inside its annual report [S3]; we have not audited its supply-chain traceability claims.

Dated: the nine-month results are out and the company's own statement is the base for our current-year numbers [S2]; the FY2026 audit is the next hard datapoint [S7]; and the free-float deadline is the next structural one [S0]. Undated but live: a resolution of the Chinese suspension [S8].

KPIs we monitor between updates: receivable days and inventory days (the value driver); the consumer segment's share and margin [S2]; the split between related-party and third-party receivables [S7]; short-term bank lines and their roll-over [S5]; and the export registration status of the company and its four largest customers [S8].

bear.narrative: China access closes for the company's customers. The regulator has suspended 38 Indonesian bird's-nest exporters over aluminium content above the 100 ppm Chinese limit and says the suspension is still in force pending negotiation with Chinese customs [S8]; four customers took 76 per cent of FY2025 sales and the largest alone took 30 per cent [S7, F10, F11], so a single blocked buyer removes a quarter of revenue. Revenue falls instead of growing and the margin gives back the nine-month gain. The cash cycle is the amplifier: receivables and inventories already absorb about ninety per cent of sales [S7, F15, F16, F17], and were Rp632.32bn at 30 September on a -Rp44.21bn nine-month operating cash flow [S5], so a revenue stall still consumes working capital while Rp495.77bn of bank debt at about 7.7 per cent [S7, S5] keeps charging.

bull.narrative: The base case already carries the witnessed nine-month gross margin of 20.1 per cent (17.7 per cent a year earlier) and the processed-nest segment's 17.0 per cent against 13.9 per cent [S2, S5]. The bull adds three points of margin ON TOP of that achieved rate, a step in line with the 3.1-point processed-nest gain and above the 2.4-point blended delta, so it is not thinner than the last actual improvement; it stops at three points because the consumer leg is contracting and no source supports a second step. Revenue grows three points above base as China access reopens for the sector [S8] and the domestic-market pivot the same article links ("Buka Pasar Lokal, RLCO Bawa Produk Sarang Burung Walet Standar Global", S8) gives the processed-nest volume an offset — already visible in nest revenue being flat year on year, Rp379.19bn against Rp379.17bn, with the suspension in force [S5, note 20] — and the phytopharmaceutical and Realfood Reserve launches [S2] add a third leg. The domestic channel is carried qualitatively: no archived source gives its volume, price or margin. Mirrored to the bear on revenue; the margin shock is +3pp against the bear's -3pp.

12-month value vs revenue growth and gross margin

adjustments.why: on the exchange's HSC list (as of 2026-10-22): out of the IHSG, the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and the MSCI indexes [konglo deck S3]
free float 13.47% must reach 15.0% by 2027-03-31 — controller sell-down or new shares inside the window [konglo deck S25]

konglo.construction: target = fundamental 12-month value (probability-weighted business scenarios, after the liquidity discount) x the probability-weighted share of today's premium kept, (price / fundamental value today)^(1 - c) over the regime scenarios; c = share of the log gap that closes within 12 months

assumptions.label: Revenue growth
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is built from the filed nine months plus a fourth quarter held at the prior year's fourth quarter: nine-month 2026 sales were Rp424.59bn [S5, F26] and fourth-quarter 2025 was Rp187.03bn (FY2025 Rp635.17bn [S7, F3] less nine-month 2025 Rp448.13bn [S5, F26]), giving about Rp611.6bn, or -3.7 per cent. We do not extrapolate the nine-month decline of 5.2 per cent into the fourth quarter because the fourth quarter is seasonally the largest of the year in both disclosed years [S7, S5]. From FY2027E the base case does NOT return to 8 per cent growth: the consumer segment, which the previous draft called the engine, CONTRACTED 34.2 per cent in the filed nine months — Rp45.40bn against Rp68.96bn, its share falling from 15.4 to 10.7 per cent [S5, note 20] — while processed nest was flat at Rp379.19bn against Rp379.17bn [S5, note 20]. The bulk of sales (89.3 per cent) is therefore not growing and the small high-margin leg is shrinking, so we model low single-digit total growth (2.0, 2.5 and 3.0 per cent) on flat nest volume and a stabilising consumer base, fading to the house long-run rate. The company's stated export and premium-product strategy [S3] and the IPO proceeds [S9, F33] are noted as upside in the bull case, not assumed in the base without a witnessed turn. The China market-access shock of November 2026 [S8] remains in the bear case.

assumptions.label: Gross margin at base input costs
assumptions.basis: FY2026E is the nine-month actual of 20.1 per cent (gross profit Rp85.41bn on sales Rp424.59bn [S5, F26, F27], confirmed in the company's own results statement [S2]), carried into a fourth quarter at the same rate rather than the full-year 18.6 per cent of FY2025 [S7, F3, F5]. The margin gain did NOT come from the consumer mix: that segment's revenue fell 34.2 per cent and its share fell from 15.4 to 10.7 per cent of sales [S5, note 20], so mix was a drag, not a lift. The gain is the processed-nest segment's own margin, 17.0 per cent in the nine months against 13.9 per cent a year earlier, plus the Rp28.5bn cost-savings programme [S2]. We hold the witnessed 20.1 per cent through FY2027E and then fade it gently as the one-off nest-margin step is not sourced to repeat and the contracting consumer leg keeps the mix against us. We do not take the consumer share to a fifth of sales: the filed trend is the opposite.

assumptions.label: SG&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: Marketing plus general and administrative expense over sales: nine-month 2026 is 4.84 per cent (Rp1.69bn plus Rp18.85bn on Rp424.59bn [S5, F26]) against 4.57 per cent in FY2025 (Rp2.64bn plus Rp26.38bn on Rp635.17bn [S7]). The absolute overhead is falling — general and administrative expense was Rp20.17bn in the same nine months of 2025 — and the company attributes the margin gain to cost control and digitalisation with about Rp28.5bn of savings [S2]. We hold the witnessed nine-month ratio flat and let it edge down to 4.70 per cent as the consumer business scales, rather than extrapolating the full savings programme, which no filing quantifies.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: share of COGS exposed to corn
assumptions.basis: Zero. Corn is not an input to this company: the LK's cost note lists raw-material purchases of Rp379.19bn (raw edible bird's nest) and Rp41.57bn (consumer ingredients) plus direct labour, shipping, rent, utilities and depreciation [S7, F13, F14]. There is no feed, corn or soymeal line in the cost of goods sold, so the agri deck does not price this company's inputs and the link is switched off rather than fitted to a correlation the business does not have.

assumptions.label: Cost link 1: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Zero, for the same reason as the exposure input: with no corn in the cost base there is nothing to pass through. Leaving the default pass-through on a zero-exposure link would silently move the margin and misstate the driver logic [S7].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: share of COGS exposed to soymeal
assumptions.basis: Zero. Soymeal is a poultry-feed input and this company processes edible bird's nest and ready-to-drink consumer products, not feed; the segment note names only processed nest and consumer goods [S7, F8, F9], and the cost note has no soymeal line [S7, F13, F14].

assumptions.label: Cost link 2: pass-through to prices
assumptions.basis: Zero, consistent with a zero soymeal exposure [S7]. The gross-margin input is the sole carrier of input-cost inflation for this name.

assumptions.label: D&A / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 depreciation of Rp14.00bn on sales of Rp635.17bn is 2.20 per cent [S7, F1, F3, F21]. This is the LK's own charge, not the pack's Rp1.03bn, which is only the general-and-administrative slice of it; the history is restated from the filing (F1, F2) and the forecast holds the last actual's ratio, rising marginally only with the capex path below. The charge is unusually low against a Rp224.89bn gross fixed-asset base because Rp34.6bn of assets are already fully depreciated [S7, note 10], which is why the ratio does not fall as capex is added.

assumptions.label: Capex / revenue
assumptions.basis: FY2025 additions were Rp32.86bn, but Rp27.00bn of that was a single land purchase and only Rp5.86bn was machinery [S7, F21, F22]; the nine months of 2026 spent Rp10.14bn on intangibles and nothing on fixed assets [S5, F30]. Recurring spend is therefore about Rp16.0bn, or 2.5 per cent of FY2025 sales, and we hold that rate. The previous draft added a step to 3.5 per cent "for the capacity the IPO was raised to fund", but no source states what the Rp105bn proceeds fund, the capacity they add or the return timing [S9, F33], so the unsourced uplift is removed. We do NOT carry the 5.2 per cent of FY2025, because that ratio is a one-off land acquisition repeated forever, which would charge Rp33bn a year against a business whose entire tangible asset base is Rp107bn.

assumptions.label: Operating working capital / revenue
assumptions.basis: The engine's FY2025 operating working capital is Rp576.05bn, 90.7 per cent of sales — the component figures (receivables Rp273.49bn, Rp84.16bn related party plus Rp189.34bn third party [S7, F16, F17], plus inventories Rp281.32bn [S7, F15], less payables and accruals) are the audited base. The nine months of 2026 are worse, not better: receivables Rp312.42bn plus inventories Rp319.90bn = Rp632.32bn at 30 September [S5, note 6], about 111 per cent of annualised nine-month sales, and operating cash flow was -Rp44.21bn [S5, F29]. The previous draft held a fixed 86.7 per cent ratio, BELOW the FY2025 actual, which mechanically released Rp24bn of working capital on a 3.7 per cent revenue decline and produced a +Rp111bn FY2026E FCFF of the opposite sign to the filed cash flow. We hold the witnessed 102 per cent flat through the forecast and the terminal year. QC round 1 (Q3) correctly objected that the previous path faded the ratio back to the audited 90.7 per cent by FY2028E, which booked an unsourced Rp31.2bn release in FY2027E and Rp12.7bn in FY2028E against a filed trend that moved the other way (90.7 per cent at FY2025 to about 111 per cent of annualised sales of receivables plus inventories at 30 September [S5, note 6]). No filing reviewed shows receivable days or inventory days falling: receivables rose to Rp312.42bn from Rp273.49bn and inventories to Rp319.90bn from Rp281.32bn [S5, S7, F15, F16, F17], and cash collected from customers is short of sales every period [S7]. With no sourced datapoint for a reversal, the neutral assumption is the last actual, flat; the release is removed rather than assumed, and the forecast therefore consumes working capital in every year.

assumptions.label: Effective tax rate
assumptions.basis: The nine-month 2026 effective rate: tax expense Rp6.66bn on pre-tax profit Rp30.75bn is 21.7 per cent [S5], against 20.1 per cent in FY2025 (Rp10.86bn on Rp53.98bn [S7]). Both sit at the statutory corporate rate, so the forecast uses the witnessed current-year figure.

assumptions.label: Cost of debt (on opening debt)
assumptions.basis: Nine-month 2026 finance charges of Rp28.39bn [S5] against opening debt of Rp490.04bn [S7] imply 7.7 per cent annualised, which is the rate carried. Finance charges are the second-largest claim on the business after cost of goods sold: Rp37.73bn in FY2025 against pre-tax profit of Rp53.98bn [S7, F20].

assumptions.label: Yield on opening cash
assumptions.basis: Four per cent, below the engine default: the nine-month statement shows interest received of Rp0.59bn on opening cash of Rp112.78bn, about one per cent annualised, because most of the balance is operating float rather than invested surplus [S5, S7].

assumptions.label: Net new borrowing
assumptions.basis: Held flat at zero: the company does not publish a debt schedule or a maturity profile beyond the current/non-current split, and nine-month 2026 net new bank borrowing was Rp5.72bn, immaterial against a Rp495.77bn stack [S5]. No source supports a refinancing or an amortisation path.

assumptions.label: Other non-operating items
assumptions.basis: Zero: other income is Rp0.59bn in the nine months (rent and miscellaneous), and the Rp6.22bn other-income line in FY2025 [S7] is not repeated in the current year, so carrying it forward would put a non-recurring item into the base case.

assumptions.label: Minorities' share of net profit
assumptions.basis: The FY2025 actual: the non-controlling interest in PT Realfood Winta Asia took Rp63.3m of Rp40.98bn of net profit, 0.15 per cent [S7].

assumptions.label: Dividend payout
assumptions.basis: Zero, and sourced rather than assumed: the only distribution in the statement of changes in equity is a share dividend of Rp25.00bn in FY2025, which moved retained earnings to paid-in capital and paid out no cash [S7, F35]; the company went public in December 2025 and the pack's dividend history is empty [S0]. With a business that consumed Rp30.72bn of operating cash in FY2025 and Rp44.21bn in the first nine months of 2026 [S7, F23, S5, F29], a cash distribution is not fundable without new debt, so the base case carries none.

assumptions.label: Change in share count
assumptions.basis: Constant. The post-IPO share count is 3,125,000,000 shares of Rp50 par [S7, S9], and no rights issue, buyback or split is announced in any filing reviewed.

assumptions.label: Terminal growth (DCF)
assumptions.basis: Four per cent, the house long-run nominal growth for a rupiah reporter [S0], consistent with the macro deck's long-run inflation and real-growth assumptions for Indonesia. It is below the observed five-year revenue rate [S7] and therefore does not flatter the terminal value.

challenges.challenge: The consumer segment — the stated engine of the base case — fell 34.2% year on year in the filed nine months: S5 note 20 shows consumer goods revenue of Rp45.40bn for 9M2026 against Rp68.96bn for 9M2025, a share of 15.4% falling to 10.7%. §3 says "the mix had moved only slightly", and the assumptions basis says the segment is "growing again to 10.7 per cent of nine-month sales". Both statements are contradicted by the source they cite, and both of the key inputs (revenue_growth, gross_margin) rest on that mix. The FY2027E 8% growth and the 20.1% to 21.8% margin path are not supported by the filed trend.
challenges.answer: Restated the consumer segment from S5 note 20: revenue fell 34.2% to Rp45.40bn from Rp68.96bn and its share fell from 15.4% to 10.7%, while processed nest was flat at Rp379.19bn against Rp379.17bn. The old mix-moved-only-slightly sentence is gone from sections 1 and 3. Rebased revenue_growth from 8% to 2.0/2.5/3.0% (flat nest plus a stabilising consumer base), and gross_margin to hold the witnessed 20.1% then fade to 19.9%, attributed to the processed-nest margin (17.0% vs 13.9%) and cost savings, not the contracting consumer mix. Re-ran the engine: fundamental value Rp104, target Rp1,142, SELL, return -49.3%.

challenges.challenge: Half the blend (PE 30% + EV/EBITDA 20%) is peer-median 4.14x and 4.69x drawn from CPIN (5.6x), JPFA (4.17x) and MAIN (3.23x) — corn-and-soymeal feed millers with 20% gross margins, not a bird's-nest processor earning a 46.4% consumer gross margin. Those two cross-checks take the fundamental from the DCF's Rp123 to Rp80 (-35%), and the lens multiplies that Rp43 difference by 12.566 into the target. The report explains the divergence as "the pack's own trailing multiples computed on a share price that ran far ahead of the offer price", but the inputs are peer medians; RLCO's own trailing multiple is 159x PE and 68x EV/EBITDA. The stated reason does not describe the calculation.
challenges.answer: Corrected section 4: the cross-checks are now correctly described as peer-MEDIAN multiples from corn-and-soymeal feed millers (CPIN/JPFA/MAIN), not the pack own trailing multiples, and the divergence is explained with the actual inputs. Because that peer set is not comparable to a bird-nest processor with a high-forties consumer gross margin, their combined weight is cut from 50% to 20% (DCF 80%), disclosed in qc_justifications weights.changed. RLCO own trailing multiple (159x PE) is stated separately. The multiple-survival test is added in section 4.

challenges.challenge: The Rp10.14bn of capitalised intangibles spent on the phytopharmaceutical programme in 9M2026 (S5, F30) is described in §1 as "an early-stage option" and is given zero value in the model. The house card requires a development project to be carried at at least its sourced sunk capex until a project value exists; zero is not a defensible mark without a source saying the spend is impaired.
challenges.answer: Added the Rp10.14bn capitalised phytopharmaceutical programme to valuation.bridge at its sourced sunk cost (S5, F30; probability 1.0), about Rp3/share, per the house development-project rule. The engine now counts it in the DCF, EV-multiple and SOTP equity bridge.

challenges.challenge: The China risk is drawn entirely from S8, and S8 carries the linked item "Buka Pasar Lokal, RLCO Bawa Produk Sarang Burung Walet Standar Global" — RLCO is opening the domestic market with a global-standard product. That is the obvious partial offset to a blocked export channel, it is in the same source, it is consistent with processed-nest revenue being flat year on year (Rp379.19bn vs Rp379.17bn), and the report gives it nothing in either the base or the bull.
challenges.answer: Credited the domestic pivot in section 2 and in the bull case: the S8 linked item (Buka Pasar Lokal, RLCO Bawa Produk Sarang Burung Walet Standar Global) is quoted and the flat processed-nest revenue (Rp379.19bn vs Rp379.17bn) is shown as the offset already visible with the suspension in force. No archived source gives the domestic channel volume, price or margin, so it is carried qualitatively and in the bull, not as a base-case uplift; the bear -13pp remains the most likely downside because four customers still take 76% of sales.

challenges.challenge: The bull shocks revenue growth and gross margin by +3pp each, but the witnessed nine-month improvement is larger: gross margin 20.1% against 17.7%, processed-nest margin 17.0% against 13.9%, operating margin 15.3% against 12.7% (S2, S5). A bull that is smaller than the last actual improvement is not a mirror of the bear and understates the upside branch, which carries 20% probability and sets the top of the distribution.
challenges.answer: Rebuilt the bull on the witnessed margin. The base case already carries the achieved 20.1% nine-month gross margin; the bull now adds three points ON TOP of that, in line with the 3.1-point processed-nest gain (17.0% vs 13.9%) and above the 2.4-point blended delta, so it is no longer thinner than the last actual improvement. Section 5 states the reason explicitly.

challenges.challenge: Related-party trade receivables of Rp84.16bn (S7, F16) are 30.8% of total receivables and 13.3% of FY2025 revenue, and the counterparties are not named. The FY2024 related-party payable of Rp70.00bn was repaid in cash during FY2025 (S7, note 29 / financing section). §6 calls related-party dealing "modest in flow terms" without the percentage of revenue that the house earnings-quality card requires, and the bear case does not carry a related-party exposure at all.
challenges.answer: Quantified and named the related-party exposure in section 6: receivables of Rp84.16bn are 30.8% of total receivables and 13.3% of FY2025 revenue. Note 29 names the counterparties - PT Realfood Karya Indonesia, PT Eling Janji Pertama, PT Hidup Melawan Waktu and PT Bahagia Elok Sentosa, all controlled by the same ultimate shareholder - and the consumer sales run through the RWA subsidiary to them. The Rp70.00bn related-party payable was repaid in cash in FY2025. The bear case now carries non-collection.

challenges.challenge: Inventory was Rp319.90bn at 30 September 2026 (S5, note 6), 35% of assets and about 258 days of annualised cost of goods sold, and the auditor names it as a key audit matter. The consumer finished-goods line is falling (Rp19.97bn from Rp21.56bn) while that segment's revenue fell 34%. §6 dismisses the KAM in one line ("the inventory is the business") and no inventory write-down appears in the bear or in any sensitivity.
challenges.answer: Added an inventory-realisability paragraph to section 5: inventories are Rp319.90bn at 30 September (F36, 35% of assets, about 258 days of annualised COGS), secure the short-term bank lines, and the consumer finished-goods line fell to Rp19.97bn from Rp21.56bn. A 10-20% write-down removes roughly Rp32-64bn of equity and is a creditor event; the bear case and the stress carry it.

challenges.challenge: FY2026E FCFF is +Rp111.06bn, of which Rp45.74bn is a working-capital release (NWC Rp576.05bn falling to Rp530.32bn) that exists only because revenue is modelled down 3.7% against a fixed 86.7% ratio. The filed nine months move the other way: operating working capital rose to Rp632.3bn (receivables Rp312.42bn plus inventories Rp319.90bn) from Rp554.8bn, and operating cash flow was -Rp44.21bn. The first and largest discounted year therefore has the opposite sign to the actual cash flow of the same period, and the report does not disclose the release.
challenges.answer: Restated the working-capital path to the nine-month run-rate: nwc_pct is 102% of sales in FY2026E (an OUTFLOW, not the old artificial release), normalising to the audited 90.7% by FY2028E. FY2026E FCFF falls from +Rp111.06bn to +Rp17.47bn after a Rp47.85bn working-capital build, consistent in direction with the filed -Rp44.21bn nine-month operating cash flow. Section 3 now discloses the build; the DCF was re-run.

challenges.challenge: The paragraph that explains the lens misstates it twice in two sentences: "0.4% of the log gap in the base regime" where the deck says 40%, and "in the bear regime the premium is kept almost whole" where the bear closes 80% of the gap and lands at Rp174, twice fundamental value. §5 also says "the shocks are mirrored — three points either way on growth and on margin" when the model runs -13pp on revenue growth and +3pp, and the regime probabilities (25/50/25) are confused with the business probabilities (30/50/20).
challenges.answer: Corrected the lens prose in section 5: the base regime closes 40% of the log gap (the old text read 0.4% because the placeholder used pctv on a 0.4 fraction), the bear regime closes 80% and lands at Rp151, about twice the fundamental value (not kept almost whole), and the regime weights 25/50/25 are stated separately from the business weights 30/50/20. The shock description now says -13pp on revenue growth in the bear against +3pp in the bull, with both margin shocks at three points.

challenges.challenge: The terminal value is defended as "a little over half of enterprise value, which we regard as acceptable given the asset-light working-capital model". This business is working-capital intensive — 86.7% of sales — not asset-light, so the stated justification does not hold. The compounder card also requires the multiple-survival test (implied exit EV/EBIT against entry) and a stated reinvestment rate x ROIIC; neither appears, and a 4% terminal growth rate is applied to a business whose moat the report calls thin.
challenges.answer: Removed the asset-light claim: section 4 now states operating working capital is about 90% of sales. Added the multiple-survival test (terminal value over terminal EBIT implies an exit EV/EBIT BELOW the entry EV/EBIT, so the DCF fades rather than expands the multiple) and a reinvestment-rate x ROIIC statement explaining why growth is low single digit. The 4% terminal growth is justified as the house long-run rate below the observed revenue rate, with the thin moat and working-capital funding noted.

challenges.challenge: The calibration gate shows FY2026E EBITDA margin at 17.49% against FY2025A at 15.68%, a 1.81pp gap, and the report never says why the first forecast year is above the last actual at that year's prices. The margin gain is attributed to the consumer mix, which is exactly the segment that is contracting.
challenges.answer: Answered the 1.81pp gap in section 3 and in qc_justifications calibration.ebitda_margin: FY2026E carries the witnessed nine-month gross margin of 20.1% (gross profit Rp85.41bn on sales Rp424.59bn) against 17.7% a year earlier, from the processed-nest margin (17.0% vs 13.9%) and the Rp28.5bn cost programme. The gain is not extended beyond the achieved rate.

challenges.challenge: The konglo.overlay QC WARN is left unanswered in qc_justifications (only scenario.symmetry and post_bs.review are there), and §6 omits three items the konglo card requires: shareholders above 5% and the affiliates behind the float, index-deletion status (HSC names are excluded from the IHSG and the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 per the registry, konglo deck S3/S4), and enforcement status.
challenges.answer: Added the konglo.overlay justification (with [S3] and [S25] citations) and the missing section 6 konglo profile: controller PT Realco Omega Investama held 97% pre-IPO and sold 625m shares (20%) at Rp168, leaving the great majority; no other >5% holder is disclosed; free float 13.47% against the 15.0% deadline of 31 Mar 2027; HSC status excludes the name from the IHSG and the LQ45/IDX30/IDX80 and MSCI indexes; the registry shows no name-specific deletion and no enforcement; dividend policy is effectively nil. The correct application of the lens is credited.

challenges.challenge: The company raised Rp105bn at the IPO (S9, F33) and the base case raises capex to 3.5% of sales "to reflect the capacity the IPO was raised to fund", but no source states what the proceeds fund, the capacity it adds, or when it earns a return. The Vietnam and Thailand entries cited from S3 likewise have no volume, timing or capital attached.
challenges.answer: Removed the unsourced capex step: capex_pct is now 2.6/2.5% of sales (the recurring rate), down from 3.5%, because no source states what the Rp105bn IPO proceeds fund, the capacity they add or the return timing. Section 3 says so explicitly; the strategy and Vietnam/Thailand entries remain as stated plans in sections 1 and 2 without a quantified return.

missing_bull_case.note: No credit for the domestic-market pivot that S8 — the article the bear case rests on — links to ("Buka Pasar Lokal, RLCO Bawa Produk Sarang Burung Walet Standar Global"), and none for processed-nest revenue being flat year on year in 9M2026 (Rp379.19bn vs Rp379.17bn) with the suspension already in force. The bull (+3pp growth, +3pp margin) is thinner than the witnessed nine-month margin gain (20.1% from 17.7%). C4, C5, C13.

missing_bear_case.note: The consumer segment's 34.2% revenue decline (Rp45.40bn vs Rp68.96bn, S5 note 20) is absent and actively mis-described; the Rp84.16bn related-party receivable (31% of receivables, 13.3% of revenue) is called "modest in flow terms" without the percentage or the counterparties; and the Rp319.90bn inventory (35% of assets, c.258 days of annualised COGS) gets no write-down sensitivity. C1, C6, C7.

assumption_realism.note: Both key inputs (revenue_growth, gross_margin) are built on the consumer segment. Its revenue fell 34.2% in 9M2026 and its share fell from 15.4% to 10.7%, while the assumptions basis calls it "growing again" and "the engine" and the report says the mix "had moved only slightly". The 8% FY2027E growth and the 20.1% to 21.8% margin path have no support on the filed trend. C1, C8.

evidence_and_citations.note: The load-bearing segment statement in §3 contradicts the filing it cites (S5 shows a 34% decline, not a slight mix move). The konglo.overlay QC WARN is left unjustified although only scenario.symmetry and post_bs.review were answered. Credit where due: the S2 figures (46.4%, 10.7%, 17.0% vs 13.9%, 28.5bn savings) and the S9 governance facts (Baiquni, Saleh, 168, 3.125bn shares, Rp105bn) all verify exactly. C1, C12.

valuation_method_fit.note: Method hierarchy is right (DCF primary for a business whose profit is not cash) and the 11.9% WACC/12.2% COE sits inside the house band, but half the blend is peer-median PE 4.14x and EV/EBITDA 4.69x drawn from feed millers, and the report explains the divergence as "the pack's own trailing multiples" when they are peer medians (RLCO's own trailing PE is 159x). No multiple-survival test, no reinvestment x ROIIC, and "asset-light working-capital model" is wrong: working capital is 86.7% of sales. C2, C10.

bias_and_tone.note: The prose overshoots the model twice in the one paragraph that explains the target: it says the lens keeps "0.4% of the log gap in the base regime" (the deck says 40%) and that in the bear "the premium is kept almost whole" (the bear closes 80% of it and lands at Rp174, twice fundamental). §5 also claims mirrored shocks of "three points either way on growth" when the model runs -13pp/+3pp. C9.

consistency_with_sector_deck.note: Correctly read: the agri deck's corn and soymeal curves are switched off at the input level with a sourced cost-note argument, since raw-material purchases are edible bird's nest and consumer ingredients. No royalty regime applies. The residual problem is the peer set the POULTRY_FEED tag implies, not the deck reading itself. C2.

conservatism_audit.note: Three departures below what the company owns or the peer set supports: the Rp10.14bn capitalised phytopharmaceutical programme is valued at zero against the house rule that a development project is worth at least its sourced sunk capex; the feed-miller multiples carry 50% weight; and the FY2026E cash flow silently books a Rp45.74bn working-capital release. C2, C3, C8.

calibration.note: FY2026E EBITDA margin 17.49% against FY2025A 15.68% (gap 1.81pp) is not addressed anywhere, and the margin gain is attributed to the very mix that is shrinking. FY2026E FCFF of +Rp111.06bn has the opposite sign to the filed nine months (-Rp44.21bn operating cash), Rp45.74bn of it a mechanical working-capital release. C8, C11.

signoff.notes: Approved. The SELL is robust: fundamental 12-month value Rp83 against a Rp2,250 price, and the konglo lens is applied exactly as the deck specifies (premium 30.35x, base regime closes 40% of the log gap, target Rp1,112). FATAL C1 is fixed on the filed segment numbers (consumer revenue -34.2%, Rp45.40bn vs Rp68.96bn; growth rebased to 2.0/2.5/3.0% and the 20.1% witnessed margin held), and all 13 challenges are answered; QC PASS with no judge issues; lint PASS with length warnings only. §6 carries the konglo table and profile (HSC, free float 13.47% vs 15.0% by 2027-03-31, no name-specific deletion or enforcement, related-party receivables quantified) and §4/§5 carry the lens. Add the dated MSCI consultation/decision and the free-float deadline to §7 at the next refresh.

bias.note: Direction is evidenced, not a cautious tilt. Fundamental value is 83.18 from the 80/10/10 blend (DCF 79, PE 54, EV/EBITDA 14) and every method sits far below the Rp2,250 quote; the 30.35x premium is arithmetic (2250 / probability-weighted 74.14), not a stale figure. Base-case drivers depart from the last actual only where sourced - FY2026E EBITDA margin 17.5% vs 15.7% actual rests on the witnessed 9M-2026 gross margin of 20.1% (S2, S5, F26, F27) and 9M revenue down 5.3% is carried with Q4 held flat, not grown; NWC is held at 102% of sales through FY2028E with no release (Q3 fix holds in the model). The 30% bear probability reflects the still-in-force Chinese suspension (S8), which cuts both ways and keeps the balance honest.

recomputed.item: FY2025A EBITDA (EBIT + DA, excluding other income)
recomputed.source: S7: sales 635.169 less COGS 517.231 = GP 117.938; less selling 2.642, G&A 26.383 and other expenses 3.417 = EBIT 85.496; plus DA 14.005 (Note 10) = 99.50, 0.1% from the model. Including Rp6.223bn other income it is 105.72 - see Q6.

S7: cash 112.782; bank debt 494.098 (short-term 158.850 plus long-term 331.195 less current maturities 305.116) gives 381.32; gap 1.1%, inside the 5% tolerance and explained by the current-maturity split.
S7 F3 sales 635.169 and S5 F26 9M-2026 sales 424.592 - the model matches the filings exactly; the consumer segment 45.40 vs 68.96 (S5 note 20, F37, F38) is restated in the report.

findings.finding: Round-1 BLOCK (a) resolved - section 4 carries the 80/10/10 weights as model placeholders (80 per cent DCF, 10 per cent each cross-check) and no residual 50/30/20 language remains in either pass of the paragraph.

Round-1 BLOCK (b) resolved - the live justifications match the engine, with 30.35x being price over 74.14 probability-weighted value and 27.1x is price over 83.18 twelve-month value; target 1,112 = 83.18 x 13.368 premium kept, and the konglo show hsc +0.05 and ff_deadline +0.05 reproduce the 0.10 adjustment and the 40/80/-5 per cent compression.
Round-1 FIX resolved - nwc_pct is 102% of sales in FY2026E, FY2027E and FY2028E (model nwc 623.9, 636.4, 652.3), so no unexplained working-capital release remains in the forecast.

Round-1 FIX resolved - section 6 attributes the HSC list, index exclusions and the 15% free-float step to the house konglo registry (as-of 27 October 2026), not to S3/S4, which are the annual report and an LK; the konglo show agrees (HSC true, free float 13.47% vs 15.0% by 2027-03-31).

The FY2025A calibration actual (15.68%) is the model's own EBITDA definition, which excludes Rp6.22bn of other income; gross it is 105.72, a 6% difference. Immaterial to the call but the reader should know the margin check is definitional.

flags.message: a.revenue_growth: bear -0.13 vs bull 0.03 is lopsided — mirror the shock or justify the asymmetry
flags.justification: The asymmetry is a discrete, sourced event, not a cautious tilt: the Chinese customs authority has suspended a tranche of Indonesian bird's-nest exporters and the Indonesian quarantine agency says the ban is still officially in force with no resolution announced [S8]. With four customers at 76 per cent of FY2025 sales [S7, F11], a blocked buyer is a step change in revenue, so the bear carries a 13-point hit. The base case now grows at only 2-3 per cent because the consumer segment fell 34.2 per cent [S5, note 20], so the bull's +3 points is a genuine upside branch rather than a restatement of base growth; the gross-margin shocks remain exactly mirrored at three points.

flags.message: expected return -51%: name the two or three sourced drivers that produce it and what today's price implies (reverse DCF)
flags.justification: Three sourced drivers produce the -50 per cent expected return. (1) The cash cycle: receivables and inventories absorb about ninety per cent of sales [S7, F15, F16, F17] and were Rp632.32bn at 30 September on a -Rp44.21bn nine-month operating cash flow [S5], and operating cash flow was -Rp30.72bn in FY2025 [S7, F23], so the DCF cannot capitalise the reported profit. (2) The cost of capital: a levered micro-cap with a concentrated register discounts at 11.9 per cent [S0], and finance charges of Rp37.73bn already consume most of pre-tax profit [S7, F20]. (3) The price: the quote of Rp2,250 is 27.1 times our twelve-month fundamental value of Rp83 and 30.3 times the probability-weighted fundamental value, while the peer-median cross-checks (PE 4.1x, EV/EBITDA 4.7x) sit 31 and 82 per cent below the DCF, so no weighting of the displayed methods reaches the quote [S0]. The reverse DCF in the sensitivity table states what growth and margin the quote requires, and the konglo lens target of Rp1,112 still leaves the stock at a -50.6 per cent return.

flags.message: method weights differ from the industry default {'dcf_fcff': 0.5, 'pe': 0.3, 'ev_ebitda': 0.2}
flags.justification: The PE and EV/EBITDA cross-checks are peer-median multiples drawn from corn-and-soymeal feed millers with twenty-per-cent gross margins [S0], not comparable to a bird's-nest processor with a consumer gross margin in the high forties [S2]; their combined weight is cut to 20 per cent so the DCF, which fits a business whose profit is not cash, stays primary. The divergence is disclosed in §4 and the cross-checks are retained as a sanity band, not as support.

flags.message: konglo lens: price is 30.35x fundamental value (premium); the base case closes 40% of the log gap in 12 months (hsc, ff_deadline); target 1,112 vs fundamental 12-month value 83 — explain it in §4 and §6
flags.justification: The lens is applied exactly as the konglo card and deck specify: RLCO is konglo:true through the HSC list, the quote of Rp2,250 is 30.3 times the probability-weighted fundamental value of Rp74.1 a share and 27.1 times the twelve-month fundamental value of Rp83, and the deterministic lens keeps a probability-weighted share of that premium, (price/value)^(1-c). The base regime closes 40 per cent of the log gap and lands at Rp645, the bear regime closes 80 per cent and lands at Rp165, and the bull regime lets the premium widen slightly for Rp2,994; the regime weights are 25/50/25 and the weighted target is Rp1,112 against the fundamental Rp83. The closing share is lifted from the deck default by 5 points for HSC status and 5 points for the 13.47 per cent free float against the 15.0 per cent deadline of 2027-03-31, both registry facts as-of 27 October 2026, not ticker sources. The result is a statement about how fast a thin float re-rates, not a second opinion on the business, and it is explained in §4 and §5 with the konglo profile in §6 [S0, S7].
